Subject: Storage connector oncall runbook and SLA sync — Pinecone / Weaviate / S3

Hi all,

Thanks for taking this on. As we discussed at the partner sync, we need a lightweight joint runbook and SLA matrix that covers the connector behavior when the vector store (Pinecone/Weaviate) is degraded and we fall back to S3-backed cold retrieval. Primary goals:

- Define incident ownership and escalation order (customer notif vs partner vs Redwood ops)
- Error budget and acceptable degraded response modes (partial results, read-only, queueing)
- On-call rota for the connector — who picks first response vs triage
- Observability signals + run metrics to include in dashboards (5xx rates, tail latency, cache hit rate)
- Recovery steps and validated postmortem template

I've attached a first-pass draft (runbook_draft.md) and an SLA matrix (sla_matrix.xlsx). Can you each review and flag any firm constraints from your side (e.g., Pinecone regional failover assumptions, Weaviate replica warm-up times, S3 eventual-consistency windows)?

Proposed checkpoint: joint review call Thursday 2026-04-16 11:00 PT. If that works I’ll send an invite and a short agenda.

Action requested from partners: review the attachments and reply with any blocking constraints or a suggested on-call cadence by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks —
Irene

Irene Choi

Subject: Re: Storage connector oncall runbook and SLA sync — Pinecone / Weaviate / S3

Hi Irene + team,

Thanks for the draft — good framing. Quick notes from Pinecone side after a 1st pass:

- Regional failover: we do automatic replica redirect in the same region, but cross-region failover is a config+manual process. We can commit to a 30-minute RTO for region-local incidents, but cross-region will need a longer window and explicit runbook steps.
- Metrics we can reliably expose: reprovision events, index-level CPU/IO, per-namespace 5xx rates, and tail latency percentiles. We recommend using the index-level 99th-percentile latency + 5xx% as primary alerts.
- On-call: we can provide an engineering oncall rotation to engage on first response (phone/pager) during our business hours (US PST/EST). For 24x7 escalation Redwood will need to own the first-line customer communication; Pinecone becomes second-line for index-level remediation.

Samira

Saw Samira's reply. Two commercial notes before we lock an on-call expectation:

1) Any formal 24x7 escalation commitment from Pinecone or Weaviate has to be mirrored in the commercial SOW (we don't want to promise customers availability we can't buy). If partners can commit to first-response SLAs during business hours that's usually enough; we stack a Redwood 24x7 front-line.

2) For the SLA_matrix.xlsx we need a clear mapping of which failures are 'connector responsibility' vs 'store responsibility' vs 'infra (S3)'. Ben, can you take the ownership column and propose a default mapping? I'll convert to a commercial appendix after we have technical acceptance.

Laura / Irene / Samira / Alex —

Thanks for the notes. I took a pass on the runbook and ownership matrix. High level:

- First response: Redwood on-call (SRE) accepts customer impact report and enables degraded mode (read-only / queued writes) where possible.
- Second response: Partner (Pinecone/Weaviate) engages within 60 minutes during business hours for index-level remediation.
- Infra (S3) incidents are owned by AWS; Redwood SRE will coordinate and provide the customer-facing updates.

Suggested on-call cadence (for the connector): 2-week rotations, 1 primary + 1 backup. Primary handles first 30 minutes of triage; backup steps in for longer investigations. If partners can provide overlap with our business hours that matches Samira's note, we should be fine without a full 24x7 partner SOW.

I added the ownership mapping into runbook_draft.md (section 3) and a short checklist for the first 15 minutes. I also created a Jira stub SUP-2387 and linked it in the doc.

Ben Carter
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
